rdf:Description.skos:description: This ticket covers the refactoring of hardcoded global variables from `draw_io_parser.py`. The goal is to move them to a central, configurable location to improve maintainability and flexibility.
rdf:Description.skos:scopeNote:
**Relevant Code Snippets:** ```python BASE_URI = os.getenv('BASE_URI', 'https://example.com')
_prefixes = { 'rico': 'https://www.ica.org/standards/RiC/ontology#', 'add': f'{BASE_URI}/Schema/Description-Listings/', 'auth': f'{BASE_URI}/Schema/Authority/', 'owl': 'http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#' }
_classes = [ "owl:DatatypeProperty", "rico:AccumulationRelation", ... ]
DEFAULT_CAPITALISATION_SCHEME = "upper-camel" DEFAULT_INDENTATION = 2 DEFAULT_MAX_GAP = 10 OWL_METACHARACTERS = ["(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}", "/", ",", ":", ".", "'", '"', ' ', '#'] ```

rdf:Description.rdf:value:
**Research and Reflections:**
The `draw_io_parser.py` script currently hardcodes a significant number of global variables that fall into two categories: pipeline configuration and ontology definitions. - **Configuration variables** (`BASE_URI`, `DEFAULT_...`, `OWL_METACHARACTERS`) control the behavior of the parser and serializer. - **Ontology variables** (`_prefixes`, `_classes`, `_object_properties`, `_datatype_properties`) define the schema and vocabulary (RiC-O) that the script operates on.
This tight coupling makes the script difficult to maintain, configure, and extend. The proposed refactoring correctly separates these concerns into dedicated modules. `TICKET-1` is the first step in this process. My analysis confirms that the variables listed in the ticket are the correct ones to be moved.
The implementation will create the foundational `gbad_core` package and populate it with the first two modules: `config.py` and `ric_ontology.py`. This work will be self-contained and will not introduce breaking changes to the existing scripts, as the new modules will not be imported until later tickets (e.g., TICKET-5) are implemented.
**Detailed Implementation Plan:**
1. **Create `gbad_core` Package Structure:** - Create a new directory `gbad_core` in the project root. - Create an empty `gbad_core/__init__.py` file to mark the directory as a Python package. <!-- <rdf:Description rdf:about="tag:jules@google.com,2025-08-02:AICODE-TODO"><skos:note>Create gbad_core package structure.</skos:note></rdf:Description> -->
2. **Create `gbad_core/config.py`:** - Create the file `gbad_core/config.py`. - Inside this file, define a `DrawIOParserConfig` class. - Move the following global variables from `draw_io_parser.py` to become attributes of the `DrawIOParserConfig` class: - `BASE_URI = os.getenv('BASE_URI', 'https://example.com')` - `DEFAULT_CAPITALISATION_SCHEME = "upper-camel"` - `DEFAULT_INDENTATION = 2` - `DEFAULT_MAX_GAP = 10` - `OWL_METACHARACTERS = ["(", ")", "[", "]", "{", "}", "/", ",", ":", ".", "'", '"', ' ', '#']` - Add necessary imports (e.g., `os`). <!-- <rdf:Description rdf:about="tag:jules@google.com,2025-08-02:AICODE-TODO"><skos:note>Create gbad_core/config.py and move configuration variables.</skos:note></rdf:Description> -->
3. **Create `gbad_core/ric_ontology.py`:** - Create the file `gbad_core/ric_ontology.py`. - Inside this file, define a `RiCOntology` class. - Import `DrawIOParserConfig` from `gbad_core.config`. - Instantiate the config: `_config = DrawIOParserConfig()`. - Move the following global variables from `draw_io_parser.py` to become attributes of the `RiCOntology` class. The `_prefixes` dictionary should use `_config.BASE_URI`. - `_prefixes` - `_classes` - `_object_properties` - `_datatype_properties` <!-- <rdf:Description rdf:about="tag:jules@google.com,2025-08-02:AICODE-TODO"><skos:note>Create gbad_core/ric_ontology.py and move ontology variables.</skos:note></rdf:Description> -->
4. **Update `draw_io_parser.py`:** - Remove the definitions of all the global variables that were moved in the previous steps. - This step will be completed as part of **TICKET-5**, which refactors the `DrawIOXMLTree` into the `DrawIOParser` and can then import the new configuration. Attempting to modify `draw_io_parser.py` now would break the script without a consumer for the new modules. <!-- <rdf:Description rdf:about="tag:jules@google.com,2025-08-02:AICODE-NOTE"><skos:note>The removal of the old global variables from draw_io_parser.py and the import of the new config objects will be handled in TICKET-5.</skos:note></rdf:Description> -->
**Human Input Analysis:** - **AICODE-ASK:** None required at this time. The task is a straightforward refactoring based on a clear plan.
